content_preview.title: NVIDIA Dynamo 1.6.0 Adds Pluggable Router Flow Control and LPX Kubernetes Components, and Deprecates the Router's Scoring Flags
content_preview.summary: Dynamo v1.6.0, published October 22, adds request-classifier plugins to its router, LPU-backed LPX components for Kubernetes, and snapshot-backed engine failover, and moves to SGLang v0.5.21 and vLLM v0.31.0.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Dynamo v1.6.0, the open-source distributed inference platform, was published on October 22. According to the [v1.6.0 release notes](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/releases/tag/v1.6.0), it is the 19th feature release and spans 654 merged PRs from 148 contributors. The notes open with pluggable flow control in Dynamo Router, LPU-backed inference on Kubernetes, and snapshot-backed engine failover.

The Herald's earlier coverage of the serving stack includes [llm-d 1.0.0](/article/...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured Briefing (698 words by script count, within 300-800). Covers router flow control, frontend, Kubernetes/LPX, planner, engine versions, breaking changes and known issues, each attributed to the release notes. Neutral tone, no AI self-reference, no quote marks other than code spans.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read snapshots source-0.html.gz (v1.6.0) and source-1.html.gz (v1.5.1) in sources/2026-10/nvidia-dynamo-160-adds-pluggable-router-flow-control-and-lpx-kubernetes-components-and-deprecates-the-routers-scoring-flags/; snapshot sanity check passed (sha256 match with manifest, key strings present: '19th feature release', '654 merged', v0.5.21, 1.3.0rc29, v0.31.0, v1.7.0, ThunderAgent, LPX components, --router-policy-config in v1.6.0; v0.5.18, 1.3.0rc25, v0.28.0 in v1.5.1). Also re-fetched both release bodies live via the GitHub API (repos/ai-dynamo/dynamo/releases/tags/...) and verified every claim against the raw markdown. Confirmed: 19th feature release, 654 merged PRs from 148 contributors; published_at 2026-10-22T22:31:45Z (v1.6.0), not prerelease; router request-classifier hook (defer, override validated scheduling inputs, suggest a worker without overriding explicit pins), deadline-ordered policy queue, ThunderAgent builtin plugin, shared worker-selection core across Frontend/standalone selection service/EPP, scoring knobs in --router-policy-config, opt-in session prefix index; frontend V2 parsers for eight families via DYN_PARSER_VERSION, /v1/rerank for SGLang cross-encoders, root-level thinking_token_budget, mutual TLS; LPX components bring LPU-backed inference to DynamoGraphDeployments (the notes never expand LPX and the article does not either; it uses 'LPU-backed' exactly as the notes do); role pod templates, DYNAMO_RANK/DYNAMO_LEADER_ADDRESS, Dynamo Snapshot failover for SGLang and vLLM, GMS Intel XPU; Planner /v1/min-endpoints and experimental Planner Gym. Engine versions verified against the right release: v1.6.0 table SGLang v0.5.21 / TensorRT-LLM v1.3.0rc29 / vLLM v0.31.0; v1.5.1 table SGLang v0.5.18 / TensorRT-LLM v1.3.0rc25 / vLLM v0.28.0. AutoDeploy removal and PyTorch as only backend confirmed. Breaking changes verified: vLLM service renames with pod/Service/dynamo_component label changes, Operator no longer adopts unowned resources, Grove v0.1.0-alpha.14 required for new multinode deployments, structural tags default on (DYN_ENABLE_STRUCTURAL_TAG=false restores), non-streaming /v1/responses no longer infers tool calls, 8-replica planner cap, scoring/selection flags deprecated in favor of --router-policy-config with removal slated for v1.7.0, policy YAML overriding deprecated flags. Known issues (SGLang stop_token_ids/min_tokens crash, vLLM max_tokens, TensorRT-LLM /v1/messages HTTP 500) match. The 'pluggable flow control' name is the notes' own wording; no experimental label is attached to it (the notes label only Planner Gym experimental, and the article reflects that). The notes contain one local A/B figure (6.21% inter-token latency reduction, #15115, unrelated to the router); the article does not cite it and does not claim that the notes lack benchmark figures, so nothing to correct. Contributor credits are not named in the article. Suspicious-pattern scan: none on either source. Sourcing is first-party only (both are NVIDIA project release pages on github.com, which is on config/source_allowlist.txt); the article discloses this under 'What We Don't Know'.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every number, flag name, env var, version string and date traces to the cited release notes. No misattributions or hallucinated quotes. The llm-d link /article/2026-10/26-llm-d-100-... resolves to an existing published article and is described neutrally; the article explicitly states it covers a different project and implies no relationship.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional; claims consistently attributed to the release notes.
editor_notes.originality: No prior Dynamo release coverage in the archive; new topic.
concerns: Single-vendor sourcing: both sources are NVIDIA's own GitHub release pages and no independent source exists; the article states this limitation.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-attributed release Briefing with no factual errors found; approved as-is. Featured candidacy: 1 - accurate coverage of a major inference-platform release for a defined developer/operator audience, first-party sourced
